correctness.rationale: For the exact number-conserving bosonic trimer with equal hopping J, thermal end baths of strength kappa and central Lindblad gamma D[n2], the closed 3x3 Hermitian second-moment equation has central coherence damping gamma/2. The displayed covariance solves all nine real stationary equations, with t=4J²+kappa(kappa+gamma) and B=t²+4delta²kappa²; the endpoint currents agree and the middle occupation is (nL+nR)/2. The Hilbert–Schmidt contraction identity for the homogeneous system leaves only a central diagonal entry, which the nonzero commutator with hopping excludes; thus stationary covariance is unique, not necessarily the full infinite-dimensional density. Number current is 2J²kappa(nL-nR)t/(t²+4delta²kappa²). Since t runs over [4J²+kappa²,infinity), its scalar derivative has exactly one maximum at max(4J²+kappa²,2|delta|kappa), giving gamma*=max(0,2|delta|-kappa-4J²/kappa), strict enhancement iff |delta|>kappa/2+2J²/kappa, and uniqueness at boundary or delta=0. Independent 25 full 9-variable numerical solves/residual checks confirmed the formula; proof is analytical.
residual_risks: Observable is excitation-number flux, NOT heat/energy flux; model assumes three bosonic modes, rotating-wave Hamiltonian, symmetric bath and hopping, and middle-site-only pure dephasing. No full-state stationary density-operator uniqueness claimed.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS. Asadian–Manzano–Tiersch–Briegel (2012) establish thermal bosonic covariance transport methods for homogeneous/resonant chains with all-site dephasing. Contreras-Pulido et al (2014) establish noise-enhanced transport for Coulomb-blockaded electronic triple dots with distinct reservoirs and dephasing profile. Neither model has the exact centrally detuned, central-only-dephased thermally driven bosonic trimer number current or its all-rate unique optimum and threshold. The noise-assistance phenomenon itself is prior art.
